Package com.im.njams.sdk

Class Njams

  • java.lang.Object
    • com.im.njams.sdk.Njams
  • public class Njams
extends Object
    This is an instance of nJAMS. It cares about lifecycle and initializations and holds references to the process models and global variables.

    bwand

        public Njams​(Path path,
             String version,
             String category,
             ClientSettings settings)
        Create a nJAMS client.
        Parameters:
        path - the path in the tree
        version - the version of the nJAMS client; may be null only if a client.version resource on the classpath provides the version, which takes precedence over this argument
        category - the category of the nJAMS client, should describe the technology
        settings - needed settings for client eg. for communication
        Throws:
        NjamsSdkRuntimeException - if neither this argument nor a version file provides a client version

      • start

        public boolean start()
        Start a client; it will initiate the connections and start processing.

        If it returns false, the instance stays inactive and all further calls that require a started instance throw an NjamsSdkRuntimeException. The SDK has already released everything this call acquired, so no cleanup is required, and calling this method again performs a new startup attempt.

        Clients that want to differentiate whether a failed startup should only withdraw the client from the runtime or terminate the runtime must use startup() instead.

        Returns:
        true if successful

      • startup

        public StartupResult startup()
        Start a client; it will initiate the connections and start processing. Does the same as start() but reports the outcome as a StartupResult, which is only needed by clients that want to differentiate StartupResult.FAIL from StartupResult.EXIT:
        • StartupResult.CONTINUE: the client continues its normal startup.
        • StartupResult.FAIL: the runtime continues without the client, i.e., the client withdraws itself from the runtime as far as possible.
        • StartupResult.EXIT: the client terminates the runtime. This is returned instead of FAIL for any startup failure if NjamsSettings.PROPERTY_COMMUNICATION_STARTUP_FAILBEHAVIOR is exit.
        The SDK treats FAIL and EXIT identically: the instance stays inactive. Reacting differently has to be implemented by the client; see the respective client's documentation for how it reacts.
        Returns:
        the outcome of the startup.
        Since:
        6.1.0

      • stop

        public boolean stop()
        Stop a client; it stop processing and release the connections. It can't be stopped before it started. (NjamsSdkRuntimeException)

        The sender and receiver are signalled independently: closing the sender marks its own ConnectionCoordinator as shutting down; separately, the receiver is signalled and stopped. For a non-ShareableReceiver, shutdown is signalled before AbstractReceiver.stop() is called, so a startup connect racing in the background (AbstractReceiver.beginConnect()) observes the flag and releases itself instead of leaking; for a ShareableReceiver, shutdown can only be signalled once the receiver is really stopped — i.e. once the last Njams instance using it has stopped it (see CommunicationFactory.removeNjamsFromSharedReceiver(ShareableReceiver, Njams), which performs the "last user" check and the shared-receiver cache eviction atomically) — since signalling any earlier would wrongly affect a receiver other instances still use. Either way, once shutdown is confirmed the coordinator's in-progress reconnect is also cancelled.

        Returns:
        true is stopping was successful.
